text: Part 3 of the question page (c014 in 2359) asks about a ko in which one side's capture threatens, the other side answers locally instead of retaking, and the capturer then needs one more move, which the other side can answer only by retaking. If that move is an approach, c014 is S[A-1KO+]; if it is an extra move inside the ko, counted as a threat, c014 is S[KO-]. Both readings need the same threats. Seven leaves in 7487, 13262, 13539 and 13959 have this shape.

In Diagram 1, the shape as in c014, the extra move is Black 11; in Diagram 2, with the colours reversed, it is White 8. Read as approaches, they make k037 S[A-1KO-] (KO−, not c014's KO+, because White also has a local threat at F19) and k033 S[A+1KO+], your own label there. Counted as threats, as the checker does now, they make S[KO-2] and S[KO+2], with the same counts.

With the approach reading, your S[A-1KO+] in k010, S[A+1KO+] in k033 and S[A-1KO-] in k105 (Diagram 3) are right, and the other four leaves take the approach form: S[A-2KO-] in k011, S[A+1KO+] in k013 and k036, S[A-1KO-] in k037. With the extra-move reading all seven change: S[KO-] in k010, S[A-1KO-2] in k011, S[KO+2] in k013, k033 and k036, S[KO-2] in k037 and k105.

Under both answers the trees of k011, k013 and k036 are off by one threat and that of k037 by two, while those of k010, k033 and k105 have the right count; in k105 Black needs two threats more than White. S[KO-3], k011's third option, comes only with counted labels in general (the approach-label decision). No option changes the site's grading: with any of them, no move in the four problems changes between correct and wrong.

Your trees are not consistent here: the approach form in k010, k033 and k105, S[KO+] in k013, k036 and k037. Two leaves are less clean: in k010 the extra move follows a further exchange and White's free capture is in a second ko, a known weak point of the label; in k011 it follows a first approach. The counts of k010, k036, k037 and k105 are decided only in the checker's narrow area; nothing decided in the wider area contradicts them.

diagrams.caption: 13539, k037, the shape as in c014. Black 9 takes the ko and threatens to kill, White 10 answers locally, Black 11 is the extra move, and White 12 retakes for free. With White's local threat at F19, Black needs two threats more than White; your tree says S[KO+].

diagrams.caption: 13262, k033, the colours reversed; your tree says S[A+1KO+]. Black 5 takes the ko. White 6 retakes after a threat elsewhere and threatens to take E19; Black 7 answers locally, White 8 is the extra move and Black 9 retakes for free. White 10 retakes after a second threat; Black 11 has none and plays elsewhere, and White 12 captures and lives. Black wins even when White has one threat more.

13959, k105, the shape as in c014; your tree says S[A-1KO-]. White 4 takes the ko, and its capture threatens to kill. Black 5 retakes after a threat elsewhere and threatens to live; White 6 answers locally instead of retaking, Black 7 is the extra move, and White 8 retakes for free. Black needs a second threat to retake: two threats more than White.

suggestion: The approach reading, the question page's proposal for c014: only one side needs the extra move, and the other side can win by winning the ko once, which is your approach ko. It keeps your S[A-1KO+] in k010, S[A+1KO+] in k033 and S[A-1KO-] in k105, and the checker's rule changes instead.
